title: Mercy After the Conquest
subtitle: The Door of the Kaaba, the General Amnesty, and the Reconciliation of Former Adversaries
summary: Standing at the threshold of the Kaaba before the assembled population of Makkah who had spent twenty years persecuting the believers, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered an immortal proclamation of general amnesty. While a narrow list of individuals guilty of active treason faced legal accountability, the vast majority were extended unconditional pardon, transforming bitter enemies into devoted companions and setting an enduring ethical standard for victorious mercy.

sections.text: At the Threshold of the Kaaba

Following the cleansing of the sanctuary, the entire population of Makkah gathered in the courtyard of the Sacred Mosque. Men, women, and elders who had spent two decades mocking, torturing, boycotting, and waging relentless war against the Prophet stood packed tightly together, their heads bowed, trembling in fearful anticipation of what fate awaited them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gripped the two doorposts of the Kaaba, looked down upon the anxious multitude, and addressed them with majesty and solemn poise.
The Prophet began by dismantling the rigid tribal hierarchies and aristocratic pretensions of pre-Islamic Arabia:

لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، صَدَقَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ... يَا مَعْشَرَ قُرَيْشٍ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَذْهَبَ عَنْكُمْ نَخْوَةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ وَتَعَظُّمَهَا بِالآبَاءِ؛ النَّاسُ مِنْ آدَمَ، وَآدَمُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ
'There is no god but Allah alone, having no partner. He fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone... O people of Quraysh! Indeed, Allah has removed from you the haughtiness of the pagan era and its boasting of ancestors! All mankind descends from Adam, and Adam was made from dust.' (Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham; Sunan Abi Dawud 5116)
The Proclamation of Pardon: 'Go, for You Are Free'
The Prophet then paused, looked deep into the sea of anxious eyes, and asked: 'O people of Quraysh! What do you think that I am about to do with you?'

Remembering his lifelong character of honesty and benevolence, they answered with trembling hope: 'We think only good: a noble brother, and the son of a noble brother!' (Akhun kareem, wabnu akhin kareem).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled with profound compassion and replied with words echoing the historic pardon of Prophet Yusuf to his brothers:

أَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ يُوسُفُ لإِخْوَتِهِ: ﴿لاَ تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾؛ اذْهَبُوا فَأَنْتُمْ الطُّلَقَاءُ
'I say to you as Yusuf said to his brothers: 'No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.' (Surah Yusuf 12:92). Go, for you are free!' (Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham; Sunan al-Bayhaqi)

In reviewing this renowned statement, scholarly historiography notes that while the exact phrase 'Go, for you are free' (al-tulaqa') is transmitted through Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Hisham, and Al-Bayhaqi rather than verbatim text in Sahih al-Bukhari, the broader historical reality of universal pardon and extraordinary clemency toward the citizens of Makkah is universally attested across all authentic traditions.
Individual Accountabilities and the Exception of Treason

Historical integrity requires distinguishing between general civic amnesty and specific criminal liability. The Prophet initially designated a very small roster—fewer than ten individuals—who were excluded from protection due to heinous capital crimes, such as apostasy combined with violent homicide, wartime espionage, or physical abuse of Muslim prisoners. Yet even among this restricted group, the vast majority subsequently sought pardon, professed genuine repentance, and were fully embraced into the Muslim community.

Among them was Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, who fled across the Red Sea toward Yemen. His wife, Umm Hakim, embraced Islam and traveled across difficult terrain to intercept him, offering him the Prophet's personal guarantee of safety. When Ikrimah returned to Makkah, the Prophet instructed his companions: 'Ikrimah is coming to you as a believer and an emigrant; do not insult his father, for insulting the dead harms the living without reaching the deceased.' When Ikrimah stepped into the Prophet's presence, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up joyfully and welcomed him: 'Welcome to the traveling emigrant!' Safwan ibn Umayyah and Suhayl ibn Amr were similarly granted safe conduct and embraced Islam with sincere devotion.

Even Wahshi ibn Harb, who had slain the Prophet's beloved uncle Hamzah at Uhud, and Hind bint Utbah, who had mutilated Hamzah's body in grief, came forward in repentance. Though the sight of Wahshi stirred deep sorrow within the Prophet's heart, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted his profession of Islam and granted him full pardon in the path of God.

The mercy exhibited at the Conquest of Makkah stands as an unparalleled milestone in the annals of warfare. No properties were confiscated, no civilian houses were looted, and no collective punishment was inflicted upon a populace that had actively persecuted the believers for twenty years. By conquering hearts through forbearance rather than intimidating minds through terror, the Prophet transformed Arabia from a fractious landscape of vengeance into a cohesive commonwealth of faith and fraternity.

references.notes: Authentic Hadith describing the general peace in Makkah, the prohibition of bloodshed within the Haram, and the pardon of repentant individuals.
